item.title: Jackson scores as Senegal move closer to 2027 AFCON
item.description: Premier League duo Nicolas Jackson and El Hadji Malick Diouf scored on Monday as Senegal beat Sudan 4-2 to virtually clinch a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations tournament. Cameroon trounced Namibia 3-0 and Benin snatched a late 1-0 win over the Central African Republic to move close to qualification for the marquee African competition. Senegal, Cameroon and Benin have 10 points each from four matches and could all be confirmed as qualifiers on Tuesday depending on the other result in their groups. Cameroon and Senegal are former AFCON champions while the furthest Benin have progressed is the round of 16 at the 2025 tournament. Jackson came to Africa last week, having scored nine goals in all competitions for Aston Villa this season. He opened the scoring in a 4-1 home win over Sudan last Thursday. He also broke the deadlock with a fourth-minute goal away to Sudan, who hosted the match in South Sudan because of a civil war in their homeland. Defender Diouf, who moved from relegated West Ham United to Brentford during the close season, doubled the lead midway through the first half. Sudan staged a second-half comeback to draw level after 75 minutes through goals from substitute Al Gozoli Nooh and Salaheldin Adil. But a late Senegalese rally saw Pathe Mboup restore the lead, then set up Paul Mendy to score in added time. – Cameroon romp – Senegal won the final of previous edition of the AFCON 1-0 in extra time over hosts Morocco last February. But CAF declared Morocco champions because most of the Senegalese team temporarily left the field to protest a penalty, which Morocco missed when play resumed. Senegal have asked the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) in Switzerland to overturn the CAF ruling and a decision is expected this month. It took Cameroon 12 minutes to score away to Namibia through Mahamadou Nagida. Goals from Ryan Fosso and Saidou Alioum in the second half completed the victory. Benin left it late to secure maximum points with debutant Ede Oloko netting in added time. The goal condemned the Central African Republic to a fourth straight loss. Elsewhere, Zimbabwe outplayed Equatorial Guinea 3-0 in Harare, Guinea beat Eritrea 3-1 in Cairo and a Jordan Ayew penalty earned Ghana an unimpressive 1-0 win over Somalia in Essipong. In the six matches on Monday, Zimbabwe were the only host nation to actually play at home. Central African Republic, Eritrea and Namibia do not have international-standard stadiums. A civil war that erupted in April 2023 prevents Sudan from playing in Khartoum and Somalia cannot stage AFCON qualifiers due to security concerns in the Horn of Africa. item.title: Budget 2027: FG moves to slash overhead costs, directs MDAs to share facilities
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief As the Federal Government prepares its 2027 budget, it is stepping up efforts to cut overhead expenditure by directing Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to maximise the use of existing government-owned facilities instead of spending public funds on hotels and other privately owned venues for official meetings. The move is part of a broader cost-saving initiative by the Federal Ministry of Finance, through its Efficiency Office (E-Office), to eliminate avoidable expenditure, improve the utilisation of public assets and ensure value for money in government operations. According to Efe Ovuakporie, Head, Information and Public Relations Unit of the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement in Abuja on Monday evening, under the initiative, “The Office is working towards establishing a coordinated system that will enable MDAs to identify and access available meeting and conference facilities across government institutions, thereby reducing the need to hire commercial venues for official engagements.” She added, “A major component of the programme is the compilation of a comprehensive directory of meeting facilities owned by MDAs nationwide. The directory, which will be published on the Federal Ministry of Finance’s website upon completion, is expected to provide government institutions with information on available facilities and make it easier to locate suitable venues. “The arrangement will also enable MDAs with under-utilised conference facilities to generate revenue by making them available to other government institutions, while reducing pressure on government overhead budgets.” Ovuakporie said the initiative aligns with the Efficiency Office’s mandate to promote value for money, reduce overhead expenditure, monitor the utilisation of public assets and identify areas of waste across government institutions. In a related development, the Office recently inspected shared government facilities across the five South-Eastern states of Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo, as part of efforts to identify underutilised public infrastructure and opportunities for cost savings. The inspection covered selected Federal Secretariats, Federal Polytechnics, Federal Medical Centres and Federal Universities. The exercise assessed the condition, availability, utilisation and maintenance of the facilities, with particular attention to areas where improved management could enhance productivity and reduce unnecessary government spending. Among the findings were under-utilised office spaces and facilities, deteriorating furniture, fittings and equipment, as well as inadequate maintenance of some offices and common areas. The inspection teams also identified opportunities to improve the utilisation of conference facilities and strengthen the organisation, storage and preservation of official records. item.title: Gunmen kill Operation Rainbow commander, one other in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa Suspected gunmen have killed a newly graduated unit commander of the Plateau State-owned civilian security outfit, Operation Rainbow, and another person in an ambush in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victims were reportedly killed at about 3pm on Monday while returning from a condolence visit to Hurti village to their community in Tadai, Manguna District of Bokkos Local Government Area. The community leader, Machief Paul, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, said both victims were members of his community. He said, “They are all members of my community. They went to Hurti village for a condolence visit and were returning to Tadai when suspected gunmen ambushed and killed them. “They were killed in broad daylight this afternoon. It is very sad and unfortunate.” Paul disclosed that one of the deceased was a newly graduated commander of Operation Rainbow, adding that the killing had thrown the community into mourning. He said, “The commander had just graduated. We are deeply saddened by this incident, especially given the security challenges our people have continued to face.” Also confirming the incident, an award-winning Nigerian conflict reporter from Bokkos, Masara Kim, said the two men were killed in the ambush while returning from the condolence visit. The deceased Operation Rainbow commander was said to have recently completed a refresher training programme for unit commanders in Jos, Kim added. Efforts to obtain further details from security authorities were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen kill Operation Rainbow commander, one other in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Oshiomhole tackles Atiku over education privatisation, says Nigeria cannot afford policy
item.description: …challenges Atiku, Obi to clarify education policies ahead of 2027 By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Former Edo State Governor Adams Oshiomhole has taken a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar over his advocacy for the privatisation of tertiary education, declaring that Nigeria cannot afford to surrender its public education system to private interests when millions of children are still denied access to schooling. Oshiomhole argued that privatising tertiary education would further deepen inequality and undermine access to learning in a country still battling a huge out-of-school population, inadequate educational infrastructure and unequal opportunities. The former governor spoke on Monday in Abuja at the unveiling of the Renewed Hope Education A+Z Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa. He questioned the rationale behind Atiku’s renewed push for private-sector control of tertiary education, recalling that the former Vice-President had pursued a privatisation agenda during his time in office. Oshiomhole also challenged Atiku and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi to tell Nigerians whether they would sustain or dismantle the education policies introduced by the President Bola Tinubu administration if allowed to govern the country. He insisted that Nigerians deserved clarity on the opposition politicians’ education agenda, particularly on policies designed to expand access to tertiary education and provide financial assistance to students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Taking a further swipe at Atiku, Oshiomhole criticised what he described as the former Vice-President’s position on using public resources to enrich friends, warning that such an approach could undermine critical social investments, particularly education. He maintained that government resources were limited and that decisions on public spending must reflect national priorities rather than personal interests. “If the money he wishes to use to enrich his friends is not diverted to paying student grants, remember that resources are limited at any point in time. That is why economics is about priorities. What is given to those students will not be available to be used to assist friends,” he said. Nigeria’s education crisis remains a major national concern, with millions of children still excluded from formal schooling despite successive government interventions. A 2024 UNICEF estimate put the country’s out-of-school children population at 18.3 million, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age, although the Federal Ministry of Education has more recently cited an estimate of about 15 million. Against this backdrop, the federal government has introduced several interventions aimed at expanding access, improving learning outcomes and equipping young Nigerians with employable skills. item.title: Tinubu’s education reforms reach 3m tertiary students, Alausa tells opposition
item.description: …Accuses opposition of misleading Nigerians, says government prioritising results over promises By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has challenged opposition politicians, particularly former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to familiarise themselves with Nigeria’s education laws before criticising the Federal Government’s policies, insisting that nearly three million tertiary students are benefiting from President Bola Tinubu’s reforms. Alausa, who accused the opposition of deliberately misrepresenting the administration’s interventions, said criticisms of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and other education policies were misplaced and failed to acknowledge the benefits Nigerians were already enjoying. The minister fired back at Obi on Monday during a briefing at the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council headquarters in Abuja, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s record in education ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a direct response to Obi’s criticisms, Alausa said the former presidential candidate needed to study the relevant legislation before making public statements about the government’s education financing arrangements. “What Mr Obi is saying is borne out of ignorance. He needs to read the law. This is the law of Nigeria,” the minister declared. He further accused Obi of misleading Nigerians, saying: “If Mr Obi wants to blame me and mislead the public and Nigerians, that tells you the kind of person he is.” At the centre of the disagreement is the four per cent development levy introduced under the Nigeria Tax Act, which Alausa said was designed to guarantee sustainable funding for the student loan scheme. He explained that 15 per cent of the proceeds from the levy was earmarked for NELFUND, insisting that the allocation was expressly provided for in the law and not an arbitrary government arrangement. The minister challenged Obi to examine the relevant provisions of the legislation rather than cast doubts on the funding structure of the scheme. Defending the broader education reforms, Alausa said the administration’s interventions had expanded access to tertiary education through student loans, improved infrastructure, increased funding and efforts to address the shortage of academic personnel in universities and other higher institutions. He disclosed that nearly three million students in tertiary institutions and another 200,000 students in secondary schools had benefited from the administration’s interventions. “We have almost three million Nigerian students in tertiary education and another 200,000 in secondary education. Today, students in every single section of our country have benefited the most from President Tinubu’s transformative agenda,” he said. item.title: Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa
item.description: By Juliet Umeh, Agency Report At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, with police yet to establish the motives behind the attacks, which occurred about 530 kilometres apart on Sunday. Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg, while nine others were killed in a shack in Jeffsville, near the capital, Pretoria. Police spokesperson, Robert Netshiunda, said the identities of the eight victims in Sweetwaters were yet to be confirmed, although some families had approached authorities to assist. “It’s still too early to tell what the motive could have been and who could be behind the shooting because we are yet to identify the victims,” he said. In Jeffsville, six males and three females were found with gunshot wounds inside a four-room shack. Police spokesperson, Brenda Muridili, said officers were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Monday, although the shooting reportedly occurred between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Sunday. No arrests had been made as investigations continued. Gauteng Police Commissioner, Tommy Mthombeni, said the killings could be linked to a shooting in nearby Saulsville last year, which claimed 12 lives and left 13 others injured. He disclosed that one of Sunday’s victims was a person of interest in the previous attack, adding that police could not rule out retaliation. South Africa has recorded several deadly mass shootings in the past year. In September, 11 people, including a pregnant woman, were killed in an attack on a house near Durban, while another shooting at a tavern claimed 17 lives. Two separate shootings in Johannesburg in June also left 24 people dead, with police linking one to rival illegal mining gangs. Two other mass shootings in December last year claimed 21 lives. Police investigations into Sunday’s attacks are ongoing. The post Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria’s inflation rate drops to 14.06% in October
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent recorded in September, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) has said. The NBS disclosed this in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report released on Monday, also showing a decline in food inflation to 19.13 per cent in October from 19.59 per cent in the preceding month. According to the report, headline inflation stood at 18.97 per cent in October 2025, indicating a 4.91 percentage-point decline in the annual rate between October 2025 and October 2026. The statistics agency, however, reported an increase in the month-on-month headline inflation rate, which rose to 0.43 per cent in October from 0.06 per cent in September. It explained that the development indicated that the average price level increased at a faster rate in October than in the preceding month. “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06%, down from 14.63% in September 2026 and stood at 18.97% in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025),” the NBS stated. The report added that the October 2026 headline inflation rate represented a 4.91 percentage-point decline compared with the corresponding period of the previous year. “On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43%, which was 0.38% higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06%). “This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026,” the agency said. item.title: INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Edo has disowned the author of a viral video, claiming to have recruited ad-hoc personnel for the commission and directing them to work for a particular political interest. In a statement issued on Monday in Benin by the commission’s Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Samuel Sunday, on behalf of the Resident Electoral Commissioner, the commission stated that the man was not its staff member. “INEC Edo declares that no one named Osayi Israel Omoroduwa is among its staff in Edo, and that no one has the power or access to recruit ad-hoc staff for the commission,” Sunday explained. He further explained that the recruitment of ad-hoc personnel was conducted exclusively through the online INECPRES platform, administered by INEC Headquarters. “The path to being an ad-hoc staff of INEC is by online application through the INECPRES platform and whoever has internet access can do so by themselves or support others so qualified to apply,” he added. He emphasised that staff members in its state offices could not influence the recruitment process, adding that the person named in the video had no special access to the platform. According to Sunday, successful applicants will undergo scrutiny by the commission and receive training on the conduct and ethics of elections. The INEC Spokesman described the online video as “an irresponsible and targeted attack” on the commission and its processes. He argued that the video was intended to undermine public confidence in the electoral process through misinformation. He, however, reaffirmed the commitment of the commission to conducting credible elections and urged the public to disregard what it described as “falsehood contained in the video”. (NAN) The post INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: We blocked channels used to siphon Abia funds — Otti
item.description: Governor attributes poor roads, dirty environment to alleged diversion of public resources By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has attributed the infrastructural and environmental challenges inherited by his administration to the alleged diversion of public resources by some politicians in the state. Otti said his administration had blocked entrenched channels through which public funds were allegedly siphoned, describing the former system as a political feeding bottle. The governor, who spoke at a two-day crusade organised by the Lord’s Chosen Charismatic Renewal Ministries at Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, said those criticising his administration were unhappy because they could no longer access public resources through the alleged channels. “Why they are murmuring is that we removed the feeding bottle from their mouths. And that feeding bottle was what they used to siphon all our resources. That was why there were no good roads and everywhere was dirty,” he said. Otti maintained that his administration would not reverse course despite criticisms, insisting that blocking access to public resources by vested interests was necessary to redirect government funds towards development. He cited road rehabilitation, improved environmental sanitation and drainage infrastructure in Aba as evidence of the changes recorded under his administration. According to him, the city has witnessed significant improvement in flood control, with floodwaters no longer lingering after heavy rainfall as they reportedly did in previous years. “Before now, there were no good roads, everywhere was dirty, the gutters were blocked, and whenever it rained, the entire place became flooded. “But I am sure that those of you living in Aba can testify that, despite the heavy rains this year, floodwaters no longer remain for long after the rains,” he said. Promises consolidation after rescue phase Looking ahead, Otti said the achievements recorded in the past three and a half years represented only the beginning of his administration’s efforts to reposition the state. He promised that the next four and a half years would focus on consolidating the gains already recorded. “What we have done in three and a half years is just the beginning of the rescue. The next four and a half years will be serious consolidation,” he declared. The governor also announced plans to improve facilities for future large-scale crusades organised by the ministry following concerns over the exposure of worshippers to the scorching sun at the polytechnic venue. He disclosed that he had directed the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development to ensure that subsequent major gatherings by the ministry were held at the stadium. item.title: Okpe leaders demand restoration of distinct ethnic status in Delta
item.description: Leaders in Okpe Kingdom have urged their indigenous people to work towards restoring the recognition of the Okpe as a distinct ethnic nationality, saying this would pave the way for the kingdom to regain its rightful status under the DESOPADEC Law, as was the case in the defunct Midwest Region and Bendel State. The elders, while reflecting on the historical position of the Okpe Union, said it would continue to push for the recognition of the Okpe as a distinct ethnic nationality in Nigeria and Delta State. They made this known in a statement signed by Professor Igho Natufe, President-General, Okpe Union (Worldwide); Kingsley Akpederin, General Secretary, Okpe Union (Worldwide); and Victor Oruno, National Publicity Secretary, Okpe Union (Worldwide). The statement read: “Since the restoration of the Okpe Monarchy on January 1, 1945, after an interregnum of over 150 years, the Orodje institution has gradually re-established itself as one of the most important centres of administrative stability in Nigeria, contributing to the socio-economic and political evolution of the country and, most importantly, to inter-ethnic relations in the then Midwest Region (later known as Bendel State) and now Delta State. “At the creation of Delta State, the then Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhoro I, became the pioneer chairman of the Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers. In furtherance of the legacy of the Okpe Nation as a rallying centre for the unity of the various ethnic nationalities in the Delta area, it is heartwarming that the Delta State Government recognised and appointed HRM Orhue I as Chairman of the Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers. In this position, HRM Orhue I has contributed to the peaceful coexistence and security of our dear Delta State.” They also congratulated His Royal Majesty, Orhue I, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, and all Okpe nationals on the 20th anniversary of his coronation, being commemorated from November 13 to 22, 2026. The leaders praised the traditional ruler for his leadership and initiatives aimed at uplifting the people of Okpe Kingdom. “Back home in the Okpe Nation, there has been notable and sustained improvement in the infrastructural landscape of the Okpe Kingdom since 2006, when HRM Orhue I ascended the throne of the forefathers of the Okpe Nation. The Okpe Nation has moved from the highest political position of Deputy Governorship it ever attained in the Second Republic to the Governorship of Delta State currently, after the position of Speaker of the House of Assembly had been occupied consecutively by two Okpe sons during the reign of HRM Orhue I.” They also commended Orhue I for ensuring that the Okpe language was officially recognised by the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council, NERDC. item.title: Plateau Council imposes curfew after gunmen burn seven houses
item.description: Residents flee Qua’an-Pan communities as tension mounts By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen set seven houses ablaze in Bong community. The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed amid reports of residents fleeing their homes, shops shutting down and commercial activities grinding to a halt over fears of further attacks. The Director of Press and Publicity to the Executive Chairman of the council, Danaan Cletus Sylvanus, announced the restriction in a public notice issued on Monday, November 16, 2026. He said the curfew was necessary in view of the prevailing security situation in the district, warning that anyone found moving around during the restricted hours would be treated as a security threat by security agencies. The council urged residents to comply strictly with the directive and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace and prevent further breakdown of law and order. The development followed Sunday’s attack on Bong community in Doemak District, where suspected gunmen reportedly stormed the village at about 9pm and set seven houses on fire. A community source, Mr Silas Bishop, who confirmed the incident, lamented the destruction and called on security operatives to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible. He also urged security agencies to strengthen surveillance and deploy additional personnel to vulnerable communities to prevent further attacks. Meanwhile, tension has reportedly gripped Doemak, the headquarters of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area, with residents said to be packing their belongings and relocating to safer locations over fears for their lives and property. As of Monday evening, shops were reportedly closed, while commercial activities remained disrupted amid growing concerns over the security situation. Confirming the attack, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Hon. (Dr.) Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the incident and assured residents that the government would not abandon them. Manship, who visited Bong community to assess the destruction, pledged government support for efforts to rebuild the houses destroyed by the attackers. He said, “Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks.” The chairman urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies. The attack on Bong occurred around the same time suspected terrorists invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several residents were reportedly killed. item.title: APC flags off 2027 campaign in Abia, Kalu targets 75% for Tinubu
item.description: …SEDC unveils 100,000-hectare agro-project, gas pipeline, industrial parks By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – The All Progressives Congress (APC) on Monday formally flagged off its 2027 general election campaign in Abia State with a rally in Umuahia, where party leaders pledged massive votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. The rally, held at the Umuahia Township Stadium, attracted party leaders, candidates and supporters from across the state, with thousands of people filling the venue and causing heavy vehicular and human traffic around adjoining streets. Leading the campaign, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, declared that Abia would deliver 75 per cent of its votes to Tinubu in 2027, insisting that the President would not need to struggle to secure the constitutionally required 25 per cent in the state. Kalu, who described the turnout as evidence of the APC’s growing political strength in Abia, said the party had about 162,000 registered members and had challenged each member to mobilise 10 additional voters for Tinubu. According to him, the strategy could translate into more than 1.6 million votes for the President. “Don’t beg for 25 per cent. Your sons and daughters in Abia State will give you 75 per cent. We have about 2.3 million voters in Abia State. We are mobilising. We are not sleeping,” he declared. He said the party’s mobilisation efforts extended beyond rallies to house-to-house, village-to-village and community-to-community campaigns. The Deputy Speaker challenged those questioning the APC’s electoral strength in Abia to await the party’s proposed rally at Enyimba Stadium, Aba, on December 7, describing the Umuahia gathering, organised within one week, as a foretaste of what was to come. Kalu also appealed to Tinubu to reconsider his earlier decision to attend only the Enugu rally during his South-East campaign engagements and attend the proposed Aba rally. Tinubu has remembered South-East — Kalu Explaining why the South-East should support Tinubu’s second-term ambition, Kalu listed the establishment of the South-East Development Commission (SEDC), stabilisation of the foreign exchange market, student loans under NELFUND, tax reforms and increased security funding among the administration’s interventions. He said the President had demonstrated commitment to the region by addressing longstanding grievances dating back to the Nigerian Civil War. Kalu also credited the administration with expanding access to higher education through student loans and supporting efforts to prevent recurrent industrial actions in public universities. He commended Tinubu for supporting his emergence as Deputy Speaker, describing the position as an opportunity to advance the interests of the South-East. item.title: Oyebanji signs three laws, revises Ekiti ₦415.5bn budget
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI – Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has signed three new laws, including the 2026 Revised Appropriation Law, the Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law and the Right of Way Law. The laws were presented to the governor for assent in his office in Ado-Ekiti by the Speaker of the State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Aribasoye, following their passage by the legislature. The 2026 Revised Appropriation Law retains the state’s total budget at ₦415.57 billion but adjusts the allocation between recurrent and capital expenditure. Under the revised budget, recurrent expenditure increases from ₦221.87 billion to ₦268.76 billion, while capital expenditure decreases from ₦193.69 billion to ₦146.80 billion. The adjustment represents a reallocation of funds from capital to recurrent expenditure to accommodate the state’s financial and operational obligations without increasing the overall budget approved in December 2025. The revised appropriation is expected to sustain government operations while maintaining funding for infrastructure, social development, economic growth and institutional efficiency. The second legislation, the Ekiti State Pension Reform (Second Amendment) Law, 2026 (No. 4 of 2026), amends the existing Pension Reform Law No. 3 of 2022 to formally accommodate the designation of a Director-General alongside the Permanent Secretary in the administrative and governance structure of the commission responsible for the Contributory Pension Scheme in the state. The amendment also makes consequential adjustments to relevant provisions of the principal law, including the composition of the commission’s board, staff administration, remuneration and allowances. The third legislation, the Ekiti State Right of Way Law, 2026 (No. 5 of 2026), establishes a regulatory framework for approving and administering permits for the installation and maintenance of telecommunications infrastructure in the state. The law fixes the maximum Right of Way fee at ₦145 per linear metre for ducts and cables and ₦700,000 per site for a Base Transceiver Station. It also requires telecommunications operators to comply with approved engineering standards, protect public safety and the environment, minimise damage to roads and public utilities, and restore affected infrastructure after installation. The signing of the three laws underscores the Oyebanji administration’s efforts to strengthen public institutions, improve the regulatory environment for infrastructure development and ensure effective management of public resources. item.title: Count me out of Awka kingship, says Jeff Nweke
item.description: …Declares interest in governing Anambra State By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA – Former governorship candidate of the Action Alliance (AA) in the last Anambra State governorship election, Ozo Jeff Nweke, has dismissed speculation that he is interested in becoming the next traditional ruler of Awka Kingdom, declaring that he has no ambition to occupy the throne. Nweke, a prominent indigene of Awka, said he was neither interested in becoming the traditional ruler nor a kingmaker, stressing that his political ambition was to govern Anambra State. Addressing reporters in Awka, he said aspiring to become the traditional ruler would not serve his political interests or his desire to contribute to the development of his people. He explained that speculations about his interest in the Eze Uzu Awka stool might have been fuelled by the construction of a large mansion, insisting that the size of his family informed the size of the property. “I want to make it clear that I am not interested in Awka kingship. Some people are insinuating that because I am building a mansion in a very large compound, that I am planning to become Eze Uzu Awka. This is not true. “I have a very large family. I am married to five wives and therefore someone who has up to 18 children should need a very large compound. It does not in any way mean that I am building a palace for Awka Kingdom,” he said. On the lingering crisis surrounding the Awka traditional institution, Nweke said the community was in an unusual situation with two individuals claiming the traditional stool. He identified the two as Eze Uzu II, whom he said was legitimately installed and recognised by the state government, and Eze Uzu III, who he said was also installed by the same kingmakers. “We have Eze Uzu II, who was legitimately installed as the traditional ruler of Awka Kingdom, and we also have Eze Uzu III. Eze Uzu II is there and nobody will take it away from him, especially as he is recognised by the state government. “Then we have Eze Uzu III, who was also legitimately installed by the same kingmakers who installed Eze Uzu II. However, since he is not recognised by government, what it means is that we have two kings in Awka,” he said. Nweke argued that if Eze Uzu II, being the older of the two, died, Eze Uzu III would assume the position, adding that speculation about his own succession to the throne was unfounded. He also pointed out that he came from the same village as the incumbent Eze Uzu II, saying there was no basis for him to aspire to succeed the traditional ruler. “My ambition is to become the gubernatorial candidate of my party in the next political dispensation. I am a politician and I want to do something for my people, and being a traditional ruler won’t serve that purpose,” he stated. Nweke, however, acknowledged that it was unusual for a community to have two traditional rulers at the same time. “But if Awka people decide to have two kings, maybe they want one to be on standby,” he said. item.title: Gas explosion rocks NNPC station in Lagos, damages school
item.description: By Esther Onyegbula & Olasunkanmi Akoni A gas explosion at a Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) filling station at Savannah Bus Stop, Command, Ejigbo, Lagos State, triggered a fire that spread to an adjoining school, damaging parts of its premises. No casualty was recorded in the incident, which occurred at about 1 p.m., as the school, Saint Lawrence Greater Height School, was closed for the weekend. The Controller-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, confirmed the incident, saying the prompt intervention of firefighters prevented the fire from spreading to other sections of the school and causing further damage. Adeseye said the agency received a distress call at 12:50 p.m. and arrived at the scene at 1:13 p.m. following reports of an explosion and an ensuing fire at the filling station. She said firefighters from the Ejigbo, Ikeja and Bolade fire stations were immediately deployed to the scene to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to neighbouring buildings. According to her, the intensity of the explosion caused the fire to spread rapidly from the filling station to the adjoining school, affecting parts of the institution’s premises. She, however, said the firefighters worked collaboratively to bring the situation under control and prevented the fire from engulfing other sections of the school. “No casualty was recorded in the incident,” Adeseye stated. She added that preliminary investigations had commenced to establish the circumstances surrounding the explosion. The incident has renewed concerns over the safety risks associated with gas-related operations at filling stations, particularly facilities located close to schools and other public institutions. The fire service urged members of the public to remain safety-conscious as investigations into the cause of the explosion continue. item.title: Gunmen burn seven houses in Plateau community
item.description: …Council chairman condemns attack, promises support for victims By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Gunmen have burnt down seven houses in Bong community, Doemak District of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area of Plateau State, in a fresh attack that has heightened concerns over insecurity in the state. The attack, which occurred at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, November 15, 2026, reportedly coincided with an assault by suspected terrorists on Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several people were killed. A community source, Mr Silas Bishop, who confirmed the incident, said the attackers stormed Bong community and set seven houses ablaze. Bishop described the attack as unfortunate and called on security agencies to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible. He also urged the authorities to strengthen surveillance and deploy more security personnel to the community to prevent further attacks. Confirming the incident, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Hon. (Dr.) Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the attack and assured residents that the government would not abandon them. Manship, in a statement signed by his Director of Press and Publicity, Danaan Cletus Sylvanus, on Monday, gave the assurance during an on-the-spot assessment of the destruction in Bong community. He said the government was committed to protecting lives and property across the state. “Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks,” he said. The council chairman also visited Zwagal community in Mangu Local Government Area alongside his Mangu counterpart, Hon. Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, where he condemned the killing of residents. Describing the attack as barbaric and inhuman, Manship said every human life was precious and that the loss of lives had left lasting pain on the affected families. “The government will intensify efforts to secure lives and property, which remains the primary responsibility of every government,” he said. He urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies for necessary action. Manship also said Governor Caleb Mutfwang remained determined to tackle insecurity in Plateau State, adding that the state government was committed to strengthening security measures. He conveyed the governor’s condolences to the bereaved families and residents of Zwagal, while praying for the repose of the souls of those killed. Also speaking, the Mangu Local Government Chairman, Hon. Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, assured residents that efforts were being made to improve network services in the affected communities to enhance security surveillance and communication. item.title: Atiku mocks presidency over alleged AI-generated rally crowds
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has taken a swipe at President Bola Tinubu over allegations of using artificial intelligence (AI) to create images of campaign crowds, insisting that the massive reception he received in Potiskum, Yobe State, was genuine. Atiku said the reception reflected growing public interest in the African Democratic Congress (ADC)’s Affordable Life campaign, while commending the Yobe State governor for allowing the opposition party to campaign freely in the state. In a statement on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice president expressed gratitude to residents of Potiskum and Yobe State for the warm reception that greeted his arrival from Azare, Bauchi State. He described the reception as overwhelming, saying the turnout and enthusiasm of residents would remain memorable. “The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart,” he said. Commending the governor for providing an opportunity for the ADC to engage voters, Atiku said equal access to the electorate was essential to democratic competition. “Democracy is strengthened when every party can meet the people freely and present its message. We appreciate the opportunity to bring our vision to Yobe,” he said. However, taking a swipe at Tinubu, Atiku suggested that the Presidency needed artificial intelligence to create the impression of large campaign crowds, insisting that the supporters who welcomed him in Potiskum were physically present. “The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate. “Our Affordable Life campaign needs no artificial crowd; the people’s presence and their voices speak for themselves,” he said. He further mocked the alleged use of AI-generated images, saying: “The Presidency’s AI must have forgotten that crowds need seats and that people do not fly. Perhaps in Tinubu’s imaginary rally, the supporters were expected to hover through the speech.” On the significance of the “Tinubu Must Go” chants at ADC rallies, Atiku described them as expressions of the people’s desire for change and a reminder of the responsibility that comes with securing their mandate. “The ADC’s Affordable Life campaign is not mere sloganeering. When I hear the crowd chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ at our rallies, I take those words personally. “They are a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility that will come with the people’s mandate,” he said. Atiku pledged to prioritise making life affordable for Nigerians if elected president in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. item.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artiste To Reach 100 Grammy Nominations
item.description: American singer Beyoncé has become the first artiste in Grammy Awards history to receive 100 career nominations, extending her record as the most-nominated artiste in the award’s history. The milestone came with the announcement of the nominees for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards on Monday, November 16, 2026, following her nomination in the Best R&B Solo Performance category for her song ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’. The latest recognition takes Beyoncé’s nomination tally to 100, further widening her lead over other artistes, including her husband, rapper Jay-Z, who previously held the record alongside her. Beyoncé entered the Grammy nominations list in 2000 as a member of Destiny’s Child, earning nominations for ‘Bills, Bills, Bills’ in the Best R&B Song and Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals categories. She subsequently built a record-breaking career across several genres, including R&B, pop, dance and electronic music, and country. This cover image released by Parkwood/Columbia/Sony shows “Cowboy Carter” by Beyoncé. Her latest nomination is for ‘Morning Dew (Donk)’, a previously unreleased recording from the sessions for her second studio album, ‘B’Day,’ released in 2006. The song was released on July 4, 2026, ahead of the album’s 20th anniversary, and later featured on its deluxe anniversary edition. Beyoncé and Pharrell Williams produced the track, which was written by the singer alongside Williams, The-Dream and Darius Dixon. Other nominees in the Best R&B Solo Performance category are Kehlani for ‘Out the Window’, Victoria Monét for ‘Let Me’, Jill Scott for ‘Pressha’ and Tems for ‘What You Need’. Beyond her nomination record, Beyoncé remains the most-awarded artiste in Grammy history, with 35 wins. A large Grammy award is seen outside the press room during the 62nd Annual Grammy Awards on January 26, 2020, in Los Angeles. (Photo by Frederic J. BROWN / AFP) She broke the record in 2023 after winning four awards at the 65th Grammy Awards, taking her total to 32 and surpassing the previous record of 31 held by classical conductor Georg Solti. She added three more awards in 2025. At the 67th Grammy Awards in 2025, Beyoncé also won Album of the Year and Best Country Album for ‘Cowboy Carter,’becoming the first Black woman to win the latter category. The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled to hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California.
